items.excerpt: Google Ads updated its Recommended Investment Strategy tab on the Recommendations page with Strategic budget allocation using Holistic and Growth modes. Holistic mode reallocates spend from underperforming campaigns to top performers for maximum efficiency, while Growth mode adds fresh budget to top performers without cutting spend anywhere else. Google wrote in the updated help document : Holistic mode : Use Holistic mode to reallocate existing spend from underutilized or less efficient campaigns to add budget to your top-performing campaigns. Growth mode : Choose Growth mode to add budget to your top-performing campaigns and not reduce spend on any existing campaigns. Hana Kobzová who spotted this change first and posted about it on PPC News Feed wrote, "The Holistic mode reallocates existing budgets from underperforming campaigns to top performers while adding additional weekly spend. In contrast, Growth mode strictly adds budget to constrained campaigns, maintaining existing budgets." Here are some other items to "keep in mind" Google wrote: Eligibility : You can access the Recommended Investment Strategy when budget constraints limit at least one of your performance campaigns…

Second, we’re introducing a new reporting feature in Google Ads to give you a clearer view of AI-driven performance. It will show a single, unified view of the Search ads journey — making it easy to see what search terms triggered your ads, which creative assets the user saw, and exactly where they landed on your website. This precise interface will help you better understand how customers interact with your business and validate the strategic value AI Max brings to your campaigns. We’ll share additional details and availability later this year.

items.excerpt: Most traffic screening runs after an ad serves, letting bots reach lead forms. Google wants server-side email validation. Does a billing credit cover the rest? Google has published a Google Ads Help Centre page stating that its invalid traffic filters do not, by themselves, stop bogus submissions from reaching advertisers' lead forms. The page places reCAPTCHA, double opt-in email confirmation and server-side validation on the advertiser's side of what the company calls a shared responsibility. PPC News Feed reported the document on September 17, 2026. Google wrote down that its anti-bot systems mostly judge ad clicks after the ad has already shown, so bots and careless people can still fill in a company's contact form. That matters for any business paying Google to find customers, because junk form entries land in sales lists and can teach Google's automated bidding the wrong lessons. Google now says checking those forms, with tools such as reCAPTCHA and email confirmation links, is partly the advertiser's job. The page, titled "Prevent invalid leads", sits under the Fix issues and Reporting issues sections of the Google Ads Help Centre. It carries a 2026 copyright line and no…

items.excerpt: AI is coming to ChatGPT ads… When creating a ChatGPT ads campaign, some advertisers are seeing this new toggle: Text Customization. Let’s take a closer look… What Is It? It’s on by default, and it reads: AI automatically generates personalized and translated versions of your ad’s headlines and descriptions, which may be shown without your individual review or approval. It’s interesting that OpenAI is making AI enhancements a priority for their beta ads product. Similar enhancements are the target of the most common complaints from Meta advertisers. But if you hoped to escape this with ChatGPT ads, you’d be mistaken. How Does It Work? What’s crazy is how mysterious OpenAI makes this. What would personalized versions of headlines and descriptions look like? We won’t know because there aren’t any more details or previews. And you won’t have the opportunity to review and approve those changes ahead of time. Of course, you can just globally turn these off for now, but you’ll need to do it with each campaign.

I’m not saying that you should use the broadest targeting with Advantage+ Placements in every case. You should prioritize a hands-off approach, but there are exceptions when some control is necessary. How you exert that control is important. Resist the urge to restrict by age to reflect your target customer. While I would generally start without any targeting inputs for age, audience suggestions won’t hurt. items.excerpt: You can turn off the new creative workflow… Meta started rolling out the new creative workflow in April. Also known as Multimedia Experience, it allows advertisers to provide up to 10 images and videos for a single ad. While I use and have generally been happy with the Multimedia Experience, I know I’m in the minority. Most advertisers hate it, mainly because it’s so buggy. Advertisers have had bugs both with ad creation and reporting using the breakdown by Media. What most of these advertisers don’t understand is that you don’t need to keep dealing with these bugs. You can turn this off and switch to the old way. How to Turn It Off When creating an ad, hover over the Media tooltip. There, you can click a link to “Return to original single media experience.” Even if you switch to single media, you can always hover over the same tooltip to switch back to multimedia if you want to in the future. Switch While You Can Presumably, you won’t be able to do this once the Multimedia Experience is officially launched, but you have an option for now. If you’re experiencing so many bugs that it’s not worth it, just switch back.

items.excerpt: Google Ads API v22 will sunset on October 7, 2026. Starting on this date, all v22 API requests will begin to fail. Migrate to a newer version prior to October 7, 2026 to ensure your API access is unaffected. Here are some resources to help you with the migration: Upgrade to the newest version Release notes To view a list of methods and services that your project has recently called, use the Google Cloud Console : Open APIs & Services in the Google Cloud Console. Click Google Ads API in the table. On the Metrics subtab, your recent requests are plotted on each graph. You can see which methods you've sent requests to in the Methods table. The method name includes a Google Ads API version, a service, and a method name, such as google.ads.googleads.v22.services.GoogleAdsService.Mutate . (Optional) Select the timeframe for which you want to view your requests. items.excerpt: It can be tough to evaluate your media strategy when key measurement tools — like real-time attribution, periodic incrementality tests, and media mix models (MMM) — conflict. In this Ads Decoded episode, Ginny Marvin, Ads Product Liaison, sits down with John Chen, Senior Director of Product Management for Ads Measurement, to cut through the noise. They discuss building a measurement stack across attribution, incrementality, and MMM, capturing longer purchase journeys with Qualified Future Conversions, and why treating media spend like planting seeds beats short-term ROAS (return on ad spend) chasing. And in a bonus episode, Patrick Gilbert and Nechama Teigman from AdVenture Media give an unvarnished look at implementing Meridian, Google’s open-source MMM. Discover how AI coding tools erase technical barriers, why data variance matters more than budget size, and how to plan your next strategic test. Watch the full episode here and the companion episode here .

items.excerpt: Advertisers have spotted a new Automatic Events option in the Settings tab of Events Manager. If you’re a good Meta advertiser who pays attention, this should look at least vaguely familiar to you. There is an old feature that’s described in almost the same way. I assure you there are differences. But if you’re confused, you’d be forgiven. Based on what I’ve been able to sort out, Meta’s made some administrative errors that make this far more confusing than it needs to be. Let’s break it down… The Old Feature As I mentioned at the top, the concept of Automatic Events may sound familiar to you because Meta introduced something very similar four years ago. This “Track Events Automatically Without Code” feature was originally found immediately below the Event Setup Tool within the Settings tab of Events Manager. Here’s how Meta described it: Your Meta Pixel can find and report on valuable website events, such as purchases or registrations, based on your site traffic, button text and page metadata. This feature can help you set up events without having to install code. You can choose to turn this functionality on or off. The New Feature The new Automatic Events feature is also found…

items.excerpt: We are updating our Google Ads Developer Policies formerly the “Google Ads API Policy”, to support developers in building robust, high-quality integrations as new AI capabilities continue to shape the advertising industry. These updates establish clear frameworks for emerging technologies that are more secure and drive better outcomes for our shared customers. To ensure a seamless transition to these updated standards, the Ads API Compliance team is actively reviewing existing integrations. Please check if your application requires updates by reviewing the policy. We will also reach out directly to developers who will need to transition with detailed guidance, technical resources and additional details. Why we are introducing these updates now As technology evolves, we periodically review our policies to make sure they reflect the current landscape. Historically, some integrations have relied on programmatic proxies , which bypass the verifiable and secure interface between end-users and Google. To help protect advertising partners against fraud and security risks, integrations now need to connect directly to Google Ads services using their own dedicated Google Cloud project. This…

items.excerpt: What’s going on here? Meta introduced Customer Lifecycle Strategy a few months ago. It allows you to define whether you want to get conversions from all audiences or only acquire new customers. When you choose to acquire new customers, you’ll need to define the custom audiences you want to exclude. But Meta is doing something weird now, and you need to be careful. Custom Audiences Automatically Excluded Immediately after selecting to acquire new customers, I can see that custom audiences are already being excluded. When I click to edit the excluded audiences, I see that several custom audiences already appear for Existing Customers. These weren’t custom audiences I manually selected. Meta attempted to predict which audiences I’d want to exclude, and it’s not even close. Not only is the list incomplete, but it includes audiences that do not match my existing customers. For what it’s worth, Meta didn’t try to do this with my engaged audience. That field was left blank. So just know that if you only want to acquire new customers, you’ll need to go through these manually. Otherwise, you’re likely to exclude the wrong audiences.
